ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in $\triangle ABC$, if $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle ACE$ are constructed with $AB$ and $AC$ as their respective sides, and $\angle DAB = \angle CAE = \alpha$, $AD = AB$, $AC = AE$, and $DC$ and $BE$ intersect at point $P$, with $AP$ connected, then what is the measure of $\angle APC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As illustrated, construct $AF\perp CD$ at point F, and $AG\perp BE$ at point G, then $\angle AFC=\angle AGE=90^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle DAB=\angle CAE=\alpha$,\\
$\therefore \angle DAC=\angle BAE=\alpha +\angle BAC$,\\
In $\triangle DAC$ and $\triangle BAE$,\\
$ \left\{\begin{array}{l}AD=AB\\ \angle DAC=\angle BAE\\ AC=AE\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore \triangle DAC\cong \triangle BAE$ (SAS),\\
$\therefore \angle ACF=\angle AEG$,\\
In $\triangle ACF$ and $\triangle AEG$\\
$ \left\{\begin{array}{l}\angle AFC=\angle AGE\\ \angle ACF=\angle AEG\\ AC=AE\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ACF\cong \triangle AEG$ (AAS),\\
$\therefore AF=AG$,\\
$\therefore$ point A is on the bisector of $\angle DPE$,\\
$\therefore \angle APE=\angle APD=\frac{1}{2}\angle DPE$,\\
$\because \angle CPE+\angle ACF=\angle CAE+\angle AEG=\angle AHP$,\\
$\therefore \angle CPE=\angle CAE=\alpha$,\\
$\therefore \angle APE=\frac{1}{2}\angle DPE=\frac{1}{2}(180^\circ-\angle CPE)=90^\circ-\frac{1}{2}\alpha$,\\
$\therefore \angle APC=\angle APE+\angle CPE=90^\circ-\frac{1}{2}\alpha+\alpha=90^\circ+\frac{1}{2}\alpha$,\\
$\therefore$ the measure of $\angle APC$ is $90^\circ+\frac{1}{2}\alpha$.\\
Therefore, the measure of $\angle APC$ is $\boxed{90^\circ+\frac{1}{2}\alpha}$.

ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer:

In $	riangle DAC$ and $	riangle BAE$,
$\left\{ egin{array}{l}AD=AB\ \angle DAC=\angle BAE\ AC=AE\end{array}ight.$,
so $	riangle DAC\cong 	riangle BAE$ (SAS).
Therefore $\angle ACF=\angle AEG$.
In $	riangle ACF$ and $	riangle AEG$,
$\left\{ egin{array}{l}\angle AFC=\angle AGE\ \angle ACF=\angle AEG\ AC=AE\end{array}ight.$,
so $	riangle ACF\cong 	riangle AEG$ (AAS).
Therefore $AF=AG$, so point $A$ is on the bisector of $\angle DPE$. Thus $\angle APE=\angle APD= rac{1}{2}\angle DPE$.
Also, $\angle CPE+\angle ACF=\angle CAE+\angle AEG$, hence $\angle CPE=\angle CAE=\alpha$.
Therefore,
$\angle APE= rac{1}{2}\angle DPE= rac{1}{2}(180^\circ-\angle CPE)=90^\circ- rac{1}{2}\alpha$,
and
$\angle APC=\angle APE+\angle CPE=90^\circ- rac{1}{2}\alpha+\alpha=90^\circ+ rac{1}{2}\alpha$.
So, $\angle APC= oxed{90^\circ+ rac{1}{2}\alpha}$.

Reasoning: According to the problem, draw AF⊥DC at F and AG⊥BE at G, then ∠AFC=∠AGE=90°. From the order of the rays around A in the figure and the known ∠DAB=∠CAE=α, one can obtain ∠DAC=∠DAB+∠BAC=α+∠BAC, and ∠BAE=∠BAC+∠CAE=∠BAC+α, so ∠DAC=∠BAE. Also AD=AB, AC=AE, therefore △DAC≅△BAE (SAS). Thus corresponding angles are equal; in particular, the angle formed by straight lines AC and CD equals the angle formed by straight lines AE and EB, namely ∠ACF=∠AEG. Look again at right triangles △ACF and △AEG: they have ∠AFC=∠AGE=90°, ∠ACF=∠AEG, and hypotenuse AC=AE, so △ACF≅△AEG (AAS/corresponding criterion for right triangles), hence AF=AG. AF and AG are respectively the distances from point A to straight lines DC and BE, so the distances from A to the two intersecting straight lines DC and BE are equal. Combined with A being inside ∠DPE in the figure, one can know that AP is the angle bisector of ∠DPE, so ∠APE=∠APD=1/2∠DPE. Next find the angle between the two intersecting lines. The corresponding angle relationship obtained from △DAC≅△BAE can be written as ∠ACF=∠AEG. Perform angle chasing at intersection point P: the angle between straight lines DC and BE satisfies ∠CPE+∠ACF=∠CAE+∠AEG. Substituting ∠ACF=∠AEG, obtain ∠CPE=∠CAE=α. Since D, P, and C are collinear, ∠DPE and ∠CPE are supplementary, ∠DPE=180°−α. Therefore ∠APE=1/2∠DPE=90°−α/2. Finally, ∠APC=∠APE+∠EPC=(90°−α/2)+α=90°+α/2.
